questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that operates the trailer brakes
A valve that shows the fuel level
A valve that limits cargo weight

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that operates the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The Johnson bar is a hand valve for the trailer brakes. It is also called the trolley valve. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause the vehicle to skid.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second trailer, the trailer height should be ____ the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: The "crack-the-whip" effect can:
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect can cause trailers to turn over. The last trailer in a combination is most likely to tip over from this effect. Know how your vehicle reacts and drive accordingly.

questions.question: If a load is placed on one side of a trailer, the trailer:

options.text: May have extra support during turns
May be easier to steer during turns

questions.explanation: Loading weight on one side of a trailer causes it to lean that direction. This increases the risk of a rollover during turns and lane changes.

questions.question: A combination vehicle has ____ air line(s).
questions.explanation: Every combination vehicle has two air lines: the service line and the emergency line.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when:

options.text: You take a turn too fast

questions.correctAnswerText: You take a turn too fast
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. To prevent rollovers, drive slowly on entrance ramps, exit ramps, and around corners. Avoid quick lane changes when towing trailers.

questions.question: Which of the following will not help prevent a rig from rolling over?

options.text: Keeping the cargo as close to the ground as possible
Driving on the shoulder of a road

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving on the shoulder of a road
questions.explanation: To prevent rollovers, keep cargo weight low and drive slowly around turns. Driving on the shoulder does not help prevent rollovers.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows a vehicle's wheels to lock up
It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up
It makes turning a vehicle easier

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops wheels from locking during hard braking. When ABS detects lockup about to happen, it reduces brake pressure to a safe level.

questions.question: If only a trailer is equipped with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: The brakes will likely not work
The trailer is less likely to swing out
The tractor brakes should not be used

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer is less likely to swing out
questions.explanation: If only the trailer has ABS, the driver still has better control while braking. A trailer with ABS is less likely to swing out of its lane than one without ABS.

questions.question: A trailer that is too high:
questions.explanation: Before coupling a tractor and trailer, check the trailer height. If too low, the trailer nose may be damaged. If too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: Before a trip, how can you check that air flows to all trailers?

options.text: Check for moving air inside each trailer.
Listen for air at the rear shut-off valve.
Feel for air at the front shut-off valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for air at the rear shut-off valve.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, make sure air reaches all trailers. Let air pressure build up. Send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer. If you hear air escaping from the rear valves, air is reaching the whole vehicle.

questions.question: What does rearward amplification refer to?

options.text: The amount of noise at the rear of the vehicle.
The number of trailers one tractor can pull.

questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect happens because of rearward amplification. If not handled correctly, a trailer can tip over from rearward amplification.

questions.question: If color-coded, what color identifies emergency or supply lines?
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded to help drivers connect them correctly. Blue is used for service lines. Red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: To check the connection between trailer and tractor.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: If the trailer drifts while you are backing, what should you do?

options.text: Return the steering wheel to the 12 o'clock position.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
Turn the top of the steering wheel opposite the direction of the drift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, correct it right away. Turn the top of the steering wheel in the same direction as the drift.

questions.question: How much space should there be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.explanation: Before a trip, inspect all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: What do you test by placing the trailer air supply control in the "emergency" position?
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before a trip. Make sure the trailer rolls freely first. Then pull out the trailer air supply control or place it in the "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly and check that the trailer does not move.

questions.question: When coupling, what should you do?

options.text: Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.explanation: When coupling air brake hoses, connect the correct pairs of glad hands. They are sometimes color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is used for service lines. Red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: After completing a pre-trip inspection, what should you make sure of?

options.text: The service line valve is closed.
The trailer hand brake is applied.
The emergency line valve is open.

questions.correctAnswerText: The service line valve is closed.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, make sure air reaches all trailer brakes. Open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves and listen for escaping air. Close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: What is the trolley valve used for?

options.text: Should only be used to test trailer brakes.
Should be used when parking uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be used to test trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Do not use it while driving because it can cause a skid. Do not use it while parking because it may release air pressure and release the brakes holding the vehicle.
